::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Nov: 20. 1863.  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS.55381 (2) P. 661
:::

Dear Madam,		

We shall have much pleasure in taking the stock of your books under our charge and publishing them for you on commission. When we have had a little experience of them and how they sell now, we shall be better able to advise and suggest something definite with regard to cheap editions or the like.

[The Trial](cmy_books/cmybook_53.qmd) we calculate could be got into 2 nice crown 8vo volumes selling at 12/-. We will give [£200](organizations/other_160.qmd) for leave to print & publish an edition of 2000 copies. We would propose that the leading should be taken out and the types made solid for a cheap edition uniform with [the Heir of Redclyffe](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd). We are willing to go on with this at once & also take charge of your other books as we said

The chief clerk of [Messrs Smith](organizations/other_161.qmd) the Great Railway people complains of the colour in which your books are bound on the ground that it fades. He recommends blue, a colour we use for [Tom Brown’s Schooldays](other_books/otherbook_352.qmd) & other books which have a large sale. 

I am, dear Madam,
Very respectfully yours
Alex. Macmillan
